#Bitcoin / $BTC 

So when should you consider going more risk on?

Historically the answer would be shortly after US midterm elections, which marked the bear market lows in each of the previous cycles.

Not saying the market sells off aggressively immediately after printing new lows this time like it did the others, but I think it's a decent bet we'll see a lot of volatility leading up to and shortly after November 3rd.

e.g. as bullish as I am here, why I don't think being in levered long positions makes sense... it makes a hell of a lot more sense to sit in spot positions you have a solid thesis for that you can keep stacking regardless of what the market does.

We're still early enough int he bull market that whether we send immediately or if we wait a couple of months to start sending, you should print multiples fairly easily soon enough by just stacking and being patient. 

And if we somehow get any sort of a dip - being liquid enough to stack your highest conviction names = a truly generational entry.

So don't gamble and risk sidelining yourself if your thesis is right - but your timing isn't.

Patient bulls will continue to win.

I think this is a very fair way of looking at it! My perception is that Zcash is winning the privacy narrative because it has the best tech. Any crack in its architecture is maybe even more damaging to its value than the less sophisticated privacy protocols out there, because suddenly it's not the perfect solution anymore.
It's true that it would still be a viable blockchain with a great development community underneath, but losing its USP would be severe in my eyes and that is why I have adjusted my risk. I do expect there will be others out there who do not take that view, but that is any speculative market; it is an aggregate of all of these understandings. If you have read my other writings you will know I am no longer a fan of Bitcoin (and its "money" narrative) given its current state. This is also why I have encouraged ZSAs to be implemented. Onchain revenue and anonymity sets are two very important moats for a protocol's standing in the industry.
